title: Continuous On-Chip Learning in Neural Networks using SOT-MRAM based CIM Architectures
problem: Implementing on-chip learning in CIM architectures requires halting inference during weight updates to avoid unintended computation, limiting throughput and energy-efficiency for real-time AI applications.
motivation: Enabling concurrent inference and learning is essential for real-time on-device AI processing in edge and IoT systems.
method: Proposes SOT-MRAM-based CIM architecture with 2R1W (two read, one write) bit-cell configuration. One read port (1R) dedicated to inference, one read and one write (1R1W) for on-chip learning, enabling concurrent read and write operations without interrupting inference.
key_novelty: Spin-Orbit Torque (SOT) MRAM-based CIM enabling concurrent read-write for continuous on-chip learning.
contributions: SOT-MRAM bit-cell design with 2R1W configuration for concurrent operations
Dedicated inference and learning paths enabling non-blocking weight updates
limitations: Evaluation at system-level simulation; practical silicon validation not discussed.
primary_theme: SOT-MRAM CIM for concurrent on-chip learning
